_about: Pew Research Center Global Attitudes Survey, Australia — Q1 'How would you describe the current economic situation in (survey country)?' (very good / somewhat good / somewhat bad / very bad). v is the share rating Australia's economy BAD (somewhat bad + very bad), the headline lane; the full four-point split rides detail {vg, sg, sb, vb}, and good/dk are the printed TOTAL Good and DK/Refused shares. This is a share-bad basis — never treat it as a net balance, and never arithmetic-merge it with the monthly lanes in data/confidence.json (index/net-balance bases by source definition). Figures are verbatim from Pew's Spring 2026 Global Attitudes topline (D_26.06.23_fielded-survey_topline.pdf, published 2026-06-23); its trend tables are the only source. TWO series sit in rows[]. series 'panel' is Pew's primary trend in the current survey mode (Life in Australia™ mixed-mode probability panel, ~97–99% online by wave, fielded by the Social Research Centre), which the topline runs back to June, 2020. series 'phone' is the topline's separate AUSTRALIA AND U.S. PHONE TRENDS FOR COMPARISON table (2008–Spring 2021) — Pew cautions against direct phone↔online comparison, so never splice a phone row onto the panel trend in copy. Both families have a 2020 and a 2021 wave (the dual-mode transition years); the two June/Summer 2020 and March/Spring 2021 rows are DIFFERENT surveys in different modes, not a data clash. chg is the change on the previous reading OF THE SAME SERIES; intervals vary (9 months in the panel transition years, 7 years 2008→2013 in the phone run), so chg is a row-to-row delta, not an annual rate. Methodology (n, marginError, designEffect, vendor, fieldwork dates) is from Pew's international methodology database (methodsDbUrl); it carries nothing for the panel-era June, 2020 or March, 2021 waves or the phone waves of 2008/2013 — those rows stand on the topline's figures alone (validatePewSentiment's KNOWN_METHOD_GAPS). hand-curated (Pew spring waves are annual; there is no extractor, and hand-entry is the right weight class), compiled 2026-10-12; not wired to any panel — the Snapshot's confidence section renders data/confidence.json and data/confidence-history.json only. Human-readable compilation: pew.txt.
